record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: For the recursively defined words Z_1 = 1 and Z_n = Z_{n-1} n Z_{n-1}, is a pattern p over an n-letter alphabet abelian-avoidable exactly when Z_n is abelian p-free?

evidence.quote: Let p be any pattern over a n-letter alphabet. Then p is abelian avoidable iﬀ Zn is p-free in the abelian sense.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the Zimin words over the positive integers recursively by Z_1 = 1 and, for n ≥ 2, Z_n = Z_{n-1} · n · Z_{n-1}, where the concatenation is read as a word over the alphabet {1, 2, …, n}.

Let A be a finite alphabet of variables and let p be a (nonempty) word over A, called a pattern. A word w over a finite alphabet Σ is said to encounter p in the abelian sense if there exists a nonerasing morphism h from A* to Σ* such that h(p) is a factor of w and, for any two occurrences of the same variable a ∈ A, the corresponding images of a are abelian-equivalent (i.e., are permutations of one another, having the same multiset of letters). Otherwise, w is said to be abelian p-free. The pattern p is abelian-avoidable if there exists a finite alphabet Σ and an infinite word over Σ that is abelian p-free.

Prove or disprove: for every n ≥ 1 and every pattern p over an alphabet of exactly n distinct variables, p is abelian-avoidable if and only if Z_n is abelian p-free.
artifact.status_search_result: Web sources confirm that an abelian analogue of the Zimin/Bean-Ehrenfeucht-McNulty characterization of avoidable patterns is not known: "abelian unavoidability still lacks a characterization in the style of general unavoidability in terms of Zimin patterns." Recent work (Carayol–Göller and others) has obtained doubly-exponential bounds for abelian Zimin encounters, but no proof or refutation of the exact "iff Z_n is abelian p-free" criterion was found.

status_evidence.title: On Long Words Avoiding Zimin Patterns
status_evidence.snippet: Abelian unavoidability still lacks a characterization in the style of general unavoidability in terms of Zimin patterns.
status_evidence.claim: No known characterization of abelian-avoidable patterns via Zimin words.

status_evidence.title: Avoiding Patterns in the Abelian Sense
status_evidence.snippet: Study of abelian pattern avoidance; characterization in general remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The general abelian-avoidability characterization is unresolved.
